title: Satie: the ending darkens
question: How does Satie change the tune’s final eight bars?
intro: Thirty-one bars return unchanged: the same piano melody, bass notes and chords. Then the last eight bars turn another way. F♮ replaces F♯, and the piece ends in D minor after its first D-major close.

scoreChanges.text: The change comes one bar in. After the shared G over bass E in bars 32 and 40, the tune’s F♯ becomes F♮ and the bass moves from F♯ to E. The chord also changes: A–C♯–F♯ becomes A–D–F–A, with an octave between the As.
The tune turns upwards: B–C–F replaces B–A–B. The left hand changes with it, replacing B–D–F♯ over low B with A–C–F over low E.
C♯–D–E rises twice in bars 35–36; E–D–C falls twice in bars 43–44. Low E stays beneath both versions, while C♯ in the chords becomes C♮, and the second bar’s F♯ becomes F♮.

Satie’s diminuendo starts on D, the second beat of bar 36; on the return it waits until C, the third beat of bar 44. The first fade ends at the chord in bar 38, the second at the final chord in bar 47.
The long F♯ in bar 37 becomes F♮ in bar 45, at the same height and for the same three beats. Beneath it, low E, the inner B–E movement and the A–D then B–D–G chords stay unchanged.
One note changes the last chord. After the same A–C–E–G in bars 38 and 46, F♯ becomes F♮: D major in bar 39 turns to D minor in bar 47. The Ds and As stay put; both chords last three beats.

listenFor: The last eight bars change the piano tune, the bass and finally the chord’s F♯, which falls to F♮.

sources.title: Mutopia 37: Satie, Gymnopédie No. 1 — Dover reproduction of the original, encoded by Evin Robertson
LilyPond source: identical repeated bars 1–31; alternative endings 32–39 and 40–47 in the top, middle and bottom definitions
